newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-MUSTER HAS NO MOTIVATION PROBLEMS-COACH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER HAS NO MOTIVATION PROBLEMS-COACH.

text.p: Clay court specialist Thomas Muster, battling a form slump on his favoured surface, was not lacking motivation and simply needed more practice, the Austrian's coach said on Friday.
The 1995 French Open champion was widely lauded the king of clay after winning 111 matches on the surface in 1995 and 1996, but this season he has been anything but a force.
Muster has lost three of the five matches he has contested on clay this year, culminating with a third round exit at Hamburg on Thursday when he fell to unfancied Moroccan Hicham Arazi 6-1 6-2.
"I don't believe Tom is suffering from motivation problems," coach Ronald Leitgeb told the Austrian news agency APA.
"Before coming to Hamburg last year, Tom already had 30 clay court matches in his legs. This year he only had three.

"But his performance is improving from match to match. What he needs now is to play in as many (clay court) matches as possible," said Leitgeb, adding Muster had concentrated on improving his hard court tennis this season.
Muster will make two more appearances in clay court tournaments -- in Rome next week and in St. Poelten from May 19 to 25 -- before the French Open starts on May 26.
